purpose: Close a previously omitted Eastern Fleet sortie that materially affects Japanese motive/ISR posture before SLEUTH: the Renown/Illustrious Ramree feint.

branch_launch_decision.why: Branch loss of Chittagong makes Army demand for pressure on the Arakan coast at least as strong as historical, but the value/risk ratio still favors a feint and training sortie over actually driving the only modern fleet carrier into the Japanese Akyab/Andaman land-air envelope.

historical_execution_anchor.event: Force sails from Trincomalee northeastward, intending to simulate arrival off Ramree at dawn 13 Feb.
Fleet continues northeast; Illustrious flies ASW patrols.
W/T deception is deliberately emitted; force turns south at 2100.
An aircraft transmits from the projected false onward position to sustain the deception while the fleet is already retiring south.
Force returns to Trincomalee after further training.

Japanese_branch_detection.cue: LIKELY_CUE_LEVEL_ONLY_CENTERED. Branch Japanese passive DF/traffic-analysis network is allowed to notice the deliberate 11-12 Feb emissions as evidence of an RN sortie toward the Bay/Arakan direction.
Japanese_branch_detection.track: NOT_MAINTAINED. The deliberate false continuation and RN turn south prevent a fresh visual/air track.
Japanese_branch_detection.why_no_visual_contact: At the 11-Feb noon position the force is still roughly 600 nm from Port Blair and over 700 nm from Akyab/Patenga; even the 705 long-range search system needs sector cueing. The RN deception points search effort toward the false northeast continuation while the ships retire south.

Japanese_reaction_11_14Feb: Shift a bounded share of 705 long-range sea-search sorties toward the projected northeast track/Arakan approach for about 24-36 hours; no contact is credited.
Raise Oyodo-group and submarine-contact-fusion readiness, but do not order a blind surface sortie.
Treat RO-111/I-166 and other surviving patrol boats as Ceylon/Bay intelligence assets as well as merchant raiders; no teleportation to the false track.
Keep a 705 contingency strike concept ready only if air/submarine recontact produces a recent fleet position; no such recontact occurs.
Do not release Suzuya/Kumano or a second Combined-Fleet surface package: the cue is deliberately ambiguous and the 3-Feb Central-Pacific carrier battle has already raised opportunity cost.
outcome: The feint succeeds operationally: Japan is induced to take the possibility of an Arakan/Bay sortie more seriously and spends some reconnaissance/readiness effort, but Britain does not expose Illustrious to a Japanese strike and Japan gains no firing solution.
downstream_effect: This is the strongest pre-SLEUTH trigger for the Japanese Eastern-Fleet suppression concept. It raises the standing surveillance/submarine priority through mid-February, but is not strong enough to prevent the later Central-Pacific emergency transfer of 705/331 elements.
